requirements.requirement: /tmp mounted on node1 with noexec, nosuid, and nodev enforced
requirements.summary: fstab entry added (tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec) and live remount confirmed via findmnt showing rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec on /tmp. Functional test placing an executable script in /tmp failed with Permission denied (exit 126), directly demonstrating noexec enforcement. nosuid/nodev were present as mount flags in findmnt output; mknod succeeded (expected, since nodev blocks device-node *usage* not creation) but the flag itself is directly observed in findmnt, which is the primary evidence for this requirement.

requirements.requirement: /dev/shm mounted on node1 with noexec, nosuid, and nodev enforced
requirements.summary: fstab entry added for /dev/shm with defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec, and live remount confirmed via findmnt showing rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec on /dev/shm. Functional test executing a script placed in /dev/shm failed with Permission denied (exit 126), confirming noexec enforcement in practice.

requirements.requirement: Hardened mount settings for /tmp and /dev/shm survive a reboot
requirements.summary: A healthy pre-restart baseline was captured (boot_id 98aa35f5..., mount options confirmed healthy). systemctl reboot was issued and acknowledged, the node became unreachable during the reboot window, then reconnected with a new boot_id (662e94b4...), proving a genuine restart occurred. Post-reboot findmnt confirmed both /tmp and /dev/shm retained rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec, and the functional execution-denial tests were re-run and again failed with Permission denied, directly demonstrating that the hardening persisted across the full disruption/restoration cycle. This transition also satisfies the independent node-restart evidence protocol for the sole managed node, node1, cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare (98aa35f5...) and after-executor (662e94b4...) boot-identity snapshots, which match the executor's observed values.

overall_summary: The executor hardened /tmp and /dev/shm on node1 with noexec,nosuid,nodev via /etc/fstab, applied the changes live, and proved enforcement functionally (script execution denied) both before and after an actual reboot with a verified boot_id change. All three material outcomes of the task — noexec/nosuid/nodev on /tmp, the same on /dev/shm, and persistence across reboot — are directly and coherently demonstrated. Operational hygiene is clean, with only an intentional fstab backup left behind and all test artifacts removed.
limitations: The nodev enforcement was validated only via the mount flag shown in findmnt; the functional test only confirmed mknod could create a device-node file (expected under nodev, since nodev blocks device semantics on read/write, not node creation) and did not attempt to open/use the device node to prove nodev's runtime effect.

Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so the reboot performed to validate persistence doubles as the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol; no additional nodes required separate restart evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All executor commands trace clearly to task fulfillment: baseline discovery, an fstab backup before editing (a safe, reversible precaution, not residue), the fstab edit itself, live remount, functional verification, the reboot required to prove persistence, and post-reboot re-verification. Test scripts and device nodes created for functional testing (cmd-a4ab5554c8bd49f9) were cleaned up immediately (cmd-08d8b645c34c4128, and inline rm in cmd-726b83ffc1994db9). The only residue is the timestamped /etc/fstab.bak.* backup file from cmd-291d184904cc4602, which is a standard, low-risk, intentional safety artifact rather than unwanted mutation. The lifecycle diff shows no unexpected changes beyond boot_id, ephemeral systemd-private tmp directories, and PID/port churn from the reboot itself, all expected. No unnecessary, broad, or destructive mutations were found.
